cues.zh: 这些微小的分子机器，此刻正在你体内运作。
cues.en: These are tiny molecular machines, and they are doing this inside your body - right now.

cues.zh: 要理解其中缘由，我们得把视野拉远。
cues.en: To understand why, we have to zoom out.

cues.zh: 每天，一个成年人体内有500到700亿个细胞死亡。
cues.en: Every day, in an adult human body, 50 to 70 billion of your cells die.

cues.zh: 它们或是受压、受损，或只是老化了。但这很正常——事实上，这被称为“程序性细胞死亡”。
cues.en: Either they're stressed, or damaged, or just old. But this is normal - in fact, it's called "programmed cell death".

cues.zh: 但为了弥补这些损失的细胞，此刻有数十亿细胞正在分裂，
cues.en: But, to make up for all these lost cells, right now, billions of your cells are dividing,

cues.zh: 基本上就是在制造新细胞。而细胞分裂这个过程，也叫有丝分裂——
cues.en: essentially creating new cells. And that process of cell division, also called mitosis --

cues.zh: 它需要一支微小的分子机器大军。那么，我们凑近看看。
cues.en: well, it requires an army of tiny molecular machines. So, let's take a closer look.

cues.zh: 从DNA说起比较好——就是我们常说的双螺旋分子。
cues.en: DNA is a good place to start - the double helix molecule we always talk about.

cues.zh: 这是DNA的科学精确描绘，由Drew Berry创作，
cues.en: This is a scientifically accurate depiction of DNA, created by Drew Berry

cues.zh: 他来自沃尔特与伊丽莎·霍尔医学研究所。
cues.en: at the Walter and Eliza Hall Institute of Medical Research.

cues.zh: 如果把两条链解开，可以看到每条都有一个糖-磷酸骨架
cues.en: If you unwind the two strands, you can see that each has a sugar-phosphate backbone

cues.zh: 与核酸碱基对序列相连，用字母A、T、G和C表示。
cues.en: connected to the sequence of nucleic acid base pairs, known by the letters A, T, G and C.

cues.zh: 现在，两条链方向相反，这在复制DNA时很重要。
cues.en: Now, the strands run in opposite directions, which is important when you go to copy DNA.

cues.zh: 复制DNA是细胞分裂的最初步骤之一。
cues.en: Copying DNA is one of the first steps in cell division.

cues.zh: 在这里，DNA的两条链正在被解开和分离，
cues.en: Here, the two strands of DNA are being unwound and separated

cues.zh: 由一种叫做“解旋酶”的微小蓝色分子机器完成。
cues.en: by the tiny blue molecular machine called "helicase".

cues.zh: 解旋酶旋转的速度简直像喷气发动机一样快！
cues.en: Helicase literally spins as fast as a jet engine!

cues.zh: 右侧的DNA链会连续地组装其互补链。
cues.en: The strand of DNA on the right has its complementary strand assembled continuously.

cues.zh: 但另一条链更复杂，因为它的方向相反。
cues.en: But the other strand is more complicated, because it runs in the opposite direction.

cues.zh: 所以它必须被环出，其互补链则逐段反向组装。
cues.en: So it must be looped out with its complementary strand assembled in reverse, section by section.

cues.zh: 这个过程结束时，你会得到两个一模一样的DNA分子，每个都有几厘米长，
cues.en: At the end of this process, you have two identical DNA molecules, each one a few centimeters long,

cues.zh: 但宽度只有几纳米。
cues.en: but just a couple nanometers wide.

cues.zh: 所以，为了防止DNA缠成一团乱麻，它会缠绕在叫做“组蛋白”的蛋白质上，
cues.en: So, to prevent the DNA from becoming a tangled mess, it is wrapped around proteins called "histones",

cues.zh: 形成核小体。
cues.en: forming a nucleosome.

cues.zh: 这些核小体聚在一起组成一种叫做染色质的纤维，进而被反复盘绕卷曲，
cues.en: These nucleosomes are bundled together into a fiber known as chromatin, which is further looped and coiled

cues.zh: 形成染色体，这是你体内最大的分子结构之一。
cues.en: to form a chromosome, one of the largest molecular structures in your body.

cues.zh: 在分裂中的细胞里，你其实可以在显微镜下看到染色体。
cues.en: You can actually see chromosomes under a microscope in dividing cells.

cues.zh: 只有到那时它们才呈现出标志性的形状。其余时候，DNA更多是散在细胞核里的。
cues.en: Only then do they take on their characteristic shape. Otherwise, the DNA is more strewn inside the nucleus.

cues.zh: 哺乳动物细胞分裂的过程大约需要一小时，所以这段影像是延时拍摄的。
cues.en: The process of dividing a cell takes around an hour in mammals, so this footage is from a time-lapse.

cues.zh: 你可以看到染色体排列在细胞的赤道上。
cues.en: You can see how the chromosomes line up on the equator of the cell.

cues.zh: 当一切就绪时，它们被拉开，分配到两个新的子细胞中，
cues.en: Now, when everything is right, they are pulled apart into the two new daughter cells,

cues.zh: 每个子细胞都含有完全相同的DNA副本。
cues.en: each one containing an identical copy of DNA.

cues.zh: 这个看似简单的过程其实极其复杂，需要
cues.en: Now, simple as this looks, the process is incredibly complicated and requires

cues.zh: 更加奇妙的分子机器来完成。
cues.en: even more fascinating molecular machines to accomplish it.

cues.zh: 那么，我们来看看单条染色体。
cues.en: So, let's look at a single chromosome.

cues.zh: 一条染色体由两条香肠状的染色单体组成，含有
cues.en: One chromosome consists of two sausage shaped chromatids, containing

cues.zh: 此前复制出的完全相同的DNA副本。
cues.en: the identical copies of DNA made earlier.

cues.zh: 每条染色单体都连接着微管纤维，由它们引导并帮助将其排列到正确位置。
cues.en: Each chromatid is attached to microtubule fibers, which guide and help align them in the correct position.

cues.zh: 微管通过动粒与染色单体相连，动粒在这里标为红色。
cues.en: The microtubules are connected to the chromatid at the kinetochore, here colored red.

cues.zh: 动粒由数百种不同的蛋白质组成，协同工作以实现多重
cues.en: The kinetochore consists of hundreds of different proteins working together to achieve multiple

cues.zh: 目标。事实上，它是你体内最精密的分子机制之一。
cues.en: objectives. In fact, it's one of the most sophisticated molecular mechanisms inside your body.

cues.zh: 动粒对染色单体能否成功分离至关重要。它会建立一种动态的
cues.en: The kinetochore is central to the successful separation of the chromatids. It creates a dynamic

cues.zh: 连接，将染色体与微管连接起来。
cues.en: connection between the chromosome and the microtubules.

cues.zh: 原因至今无人能解释，微管的一端不断组装，
cues.en: For a reason no one's yet been able to figure out, the microtubules are constantly being built at one end

cues.zh: 另一端则不断解聚。
cues.en: and deconstructed at the other.

cues.zh: 染色体尚未准备好时，动粒会向细胞其他部分发出化学“停止”信号，
cues.en: While the chromosome is still getting ready, the kinetochore sends out a chemical "stop" signal

cues.zh: 这里用红色分子表示，
cues.en: to the rest of the cell, shown here by the red molecules,

cues.zh: 意思是：“这条染色体还没准备好分裂。”
cues.en: basically saying, "this chromosome is not yet ready to divide."

cues.zh: 动粒还会通过机械方式感知张力。
cues.en: The kinetochore also mechanically senses tension.

cues.zh: 当张力恰到好处，位置正确、连接牢固时，
cues.en: When the tension is just right, and the position and attachment are correct,

cues.zh: 所有蛋白质都会准备就绪，这里用绿色表示。
cues.en: all the proteins get ready, shown here by turning green.

cues.zh: 此时，停止信号的广播系统并没有关闭！
cues.en: At this point, the stop signal broadcasting system is not switched off!

cues.zh: 相反，它真的会被动力蛋白马达沿着微管从动粒上拖走，
cues.en: Instead, it is literally carried away from the kinetochore, down the microtubules,

cues.zh: 这就是动力蛋白马达——那个会走路的家伙。
cues.en: by a dynein motor - that's the walking guy.

cues.zh: 它实际看起来就是这样：长着长长的“腿”，能绕开障碍物，跨过驱动蛋白，
cues.en: This is really what it looks like: it has long "legs" so it can avoid obstacles and step over the kinesins,

cues.zh: 这些分子马达会朝相反方向行走。
cues.en: molecular motors that walk in the opposite direction.

cues.zh: 我个人对这些微小的分子机器惊叹不已，它们竟能
cues.en: Personally, I'm astounded by these tiny molecular machines, how they're able to

cues.zh: 就在此刻，在你的体内数十亿次地稳定、精准地完成各自的工作。
cues.en: routinely and faithfully execute their functions billions of times over inside your body at this exact instant.

cues.zh: 我也很佩服那些科学家，他们揭开了其中的奥秘，
cues.en: I'm also amazed by the scientists who were able to work out how this happens

cues.zh: 研究得如此透彻，才能像这段视频里的动画那样，把它们逼真地呈现出来。
cues.en: in such detail that we could create realistic depictions of them, like you saw in the animations in this video.

cues.zh: 不过，也许最令人惊叹的是，还有那么多未知等待我们去发现，比如，
cues.en: But, perhaps, the most amazing thing is just how much is left to be discovered, like,

cues.zh: 弄清楚姐妹染色单体究竟是如何被拉向细胞两端的。
cues.en: figuring out how exactly the chromatids are pulled to opposite ends of the cell.

cues.zh: 我们不知道的依然还有很多。
cues.en: There is still so much that we don't quite know.

cues.zh: 最让我兴奋的是，几十年来在科幻小说里，
cues.en: You know, what I find exciting is, that in science fiction, for decades,

cues.zh: 我们总在描写能注射进血液、治愈疾病的微型纳米机器人。
cues.en: we've been writing about tiny nanobots that will be injected into our blood streams that can heal us.

cues.zh: 而我们体内这些微型分子机器的存在表明，
cues.en: But, what this suggests, the existence of these tiny molecular machines inside us,

cues.zh: 并没有什么物理极限会阻碍这一构想。因此我认为未来很有可能，
cues.en: it suggests that there isn't a physical limit that would prevent that. And so, I think it's pretty likely that, in future,

cues.zh: 我们能够研制出自己的微型分子机器，
cues.en: we will be able to develop our own tiny molecular machines

cues.zh: 它们修复我们身体的效果，甚至会超越人体自身的修复能力。
cues.en: that will be able to repair our bodies better than they can repair themselves.
